objective: Create the platform repository skeleton described by the P0.2 design of the guide repository: one workspace, the layout every later package lands in, the module registry, the seven dependency rules generated from it, the migration lint, a boundary suite that proves both fire, the charter, the continuity records and their schemas, and the CI skeleton. Revised after an independent peer review returned REVISION_REQUIRED with four blockers.
completed_scope: One pnpm workspace with the top-level layout the P0.2 design draws
modules/modules.yaml registering all 30 candidate modules of the ARCH-001 capability map, grouped platform, brokerage, financial and integration, plus platform-configuration from the P0.12 design
Four module packages, tenancy, identity-access, audit and platform-configuration, each with a public contract and a private internal half; every exported function throws
packages/contracts and packages/observability, which import no module; services/api, which imports contracts only
scripts/registry.mjs, a strict dependency-free reader that refuses a malformed registry, an unknown top-level key or an unknown field with a line number

scripts/boundary-rules.mjs and scripts/generate-boundary-rules.mjs, generating .dependency-cruiser.cjs and tsconfig.paths.json from the registry, stamped with the registry SHA-256 and compared by --check
scripts/migration-lint.mjs enforcing M1 to M6 over double-quoted identifiers, unqualified names, search_path, plural domain words and nested directories
scripts/mutation-check.mjs, which loosens each rule in turn and requires the suite to go red
scripts/check-module-packages.mjs, with its own test suite
scripts/validate_continuity.py, fail-closed, with gates and authority enumerated in the schema rather than left as bare objects
tests/boundaries with a fixture workspace and fixture migrations, one violation shape per fixture, asserted on the message rather than the rule name alone
badf/ with five registries and three records; schemas/ with five JSON schemas
AGENTS.md, the charter carried from the guide repository and revised for a repository that ships software
.github/workflows/ci.yml running the same eight commands a developer runs

DEC-002 the seven rules are generated from the registry and a hand edit fails the build
DEC-003 the registry reader is a strict purpose-built parser, not a YAML library
DEC-004 negative control 6 and every runtime control are declared non-coverage, not passed
DEC-005 the broker policy module is registered as policy-record, not policy
DEC-006 mutation testing becomes a committed, required check rather than a one-off review technique
DEC-007 gates and authority are enumerated in the schema, so recording a gate or widening a grant is a reviewed schema change and not a data edit
DEC-008 the migration lint normalises quoting and refuses unqualified names, and its docstring now states its real limits rather than a conservatism it did not have
assumptions: ASSUMED: the modular monolith of ARCH-001 section 4.1, with the seven dependency rules and one schema per module. ADR-001 decides this and is DRAFT_REQUIRED.
ASSUMED: the candidate modules of the ARCH-001 capability map are the registry entries. Whether each is a bounded context, a subdomain or an aggregate is BIZTRUST-DOMAIN-001's decision.
ASSUMED: dependency-cruiser as the checker. The rules are generated, so a different checker consumes the same registry.
ASSUMED: the migration lint is a deterministic script under scripts/, per P0.2 open question 5. It is a text check over SQL and its blind spots are listed under declared_non_coverage.
ASSUMED: GitHub as the host, with the branch protection the guide charter describes.
blockers: BT-G0 is unrecorded. ARCH-001 is a draft, and FOUNDATION_SEQUENCE.md slice S01 needs five human review seats that are unfilled. No P0 epic may be implemented until an architecture authority records it.
ADR-001, ADR-004, ADR-005, ADR-010 and ADR-011 are all DRAFT_REQUIRED. The rules in this repository are the proposal of a design at IN_REVIEW.
The repository administrator seat is unfilled, so main is unprotected and negative control 6 cannot be observed.

The peer review returned REVISION_REQUIRED. Its four blockers are addressed on this branch, but a re-review of the revised head has not happened, and the reviewer, not the implementer, decides whether the revision closes them.
authority_status: The scaffold was built under a direct operator instruction, recorded in badf/authority.yaml under granted.repository_scaffold. That is an operator instruction recorded by an agent; it is NOT the expiring implementation grant from a business authority seat that the P0.2 design requires. Every other authority in that file is NOT_GRANTED, and the schema now pins those values so a grant cannot be forged by editing a data file.
next_action: Fill the repository administrator seat and record branch protection on main, so that negative control 6 becomes observable and every later package merges through a required check.
recovery: Read AGENTS.md, then badf/authority.yaml, then badf/current-state.json and badf/next-actions.json. The branch is motor/p0.2/repository-and-boundaries off 062a0f7c1b350e4af695978b238b28e323b7d0e0 on main. First safe command: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, then pnpm verify, which runs all eight checks above in order. All eight pass on this head. If any fails, the tree has diverged from this checkpoint and the answer is RECOVERY_REQUIRED, not a fix.
declared_non_coverage: Negative control 6 of the P0.2 design: a push straight to main and a merge with a failing check. Needs branch protection, which is a human record. Unobserved.
The runtime half of every control. Nothing runs: there is no server, no database and no configuration.

The migration lint is a text check over SQL, not a parser. It handles double-quoted identifiers, unqualified names, search_path and plurals; it CANNOT see through a dollar-quoted function body, a DO block, dynamic SQL built at runtime, or an extension that creates objects as a side effect. An earlier version of this file called the lint conservative by design, which was affirmatively wrong.

Rule 7's outbound host allow-list does not exist. The P0.2 design makes it a check of its own and control 10's second half a CI check; neither is implemented, and apps/ contains only a README, so rule 7 binds nothing outside the fixture. This is a CI-side gap, not covered by the runtime-control disclaimer above.
The contract lint over openapi/ and events/. Both directories are reserved and empty; the rules are P0.8 and P0.9.
The observability tests. The baseline is P0.11.
The security proof suite over tests/security/. The BT-G1 matrix needs BT-G0 first.
No fixture proves the typecheck fails, so the compiler is an unwitnessed instrument.

CI runs one Verify job with sequential steps, not the nine independently required checks the design names, and there is no Build job. The merge-blocking effect is equivalent; the divergence is recorded rather than hidden.

The mutation check covers the dependency rules and the migration lint. It does NOT mutate the record validator, the registry reader or the module-package check, so those three are tested by their own suites but not mutation-tested.
Rules 1 and 2 are generated per module; the fixture exercises one instance of each family, not all four.

The design's control 7 says the boundary check's GENERATION step catches a package with no registry row. It does not; a separate script does. Different instrument from the one specified, recorded here rather than glossed.
